description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative. Choose your own model and sandbox.
readme_content:
# Rakazo

[English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](./README.ja.md)

[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/elie222/rakazo?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&color=2563EB)](https://github.com/elie222/rakazo/stargazers)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20the%20community-5865F2?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h)
[![Download on the App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App%20Store-Download%20for%20iPhone-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099)
[![Get Android on Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Play-Get%20the%20app-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app)

![Rakazo — AI teammates you actually own](./docs/readme-hero.png)

Rakazo is an open source AI agent for persistent teammates, and a self-hosted AI assistant you
can run on your own machine. It is available on the web, as an Electron desktop app, and on
[iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099) and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app). Bring your own model
and computer provider, or run the complete stack locally.

It is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct,
OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet.

Rakazo is in beta. Learn more at [rakazo.com](https://rakazo.com).

## Features

- Persistent bots with their own conversations, memory, routines, and history
- Voice mode: speak replies, dictate, and call a bot. Bring your own ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Cartesia, or Fish Audio key, or use a Mac server's installed voices
- Shared Team Computers and isolated Private computers
- Browser, terminal, file, and graphical desktop access
- Bots that can delegate to peer bots or short-lived subagents
- Bring-your-own model credentials through Pi
- App integrations through Composio or Pipedream Connect, plus user-installed Treg, remote MCP, and OpenAPI tool sources
- Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, Boat, and trusted local-computer support

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dccdeddb-2134-4a56-8eed-b2e591736b1c

## Thanks

- [PromptLayer](https://promptlayer.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)
- [Inbox Zero](https://getinboxzero.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)
- [ConnectorMap](https://connectormap.luinbytes.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)
- [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)
- [Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)
- [Snyk](https://snyk.io/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme)

## Stack

- TypeScript
- React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS
- Electron and Expo
- Hono and oRPC
- PostgreSQL and Prisma
- Better Auth
- Graphile Worker
- Pi
- Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, and Boat
- Composio, Pipedream Connect, MCP, and OpenAPI integrations

## Quick start (published images)

You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install.

```bash
mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo &&
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh &&
bash install-images.sh
```

The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo.
It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun.

Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model.
Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, or `railway`
with the matching API key.

Default image tag is `edge` (main builds, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). Details and tags:
[self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout).

On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip
existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap
script URL — see
[Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads).

For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md).

## Run on a server

Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from
the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser.

```bash
bash install-images.sh --prepare-only
# edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain
bash install-images.sh
```

Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment)
covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter
the `https://` address.

Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md).

## Local development (source checkout)

You need Node.js 22.22.2 or newer in the 22.x line, Node.js 24.x, or Node.js 26+;
pnpm 9; and Docker. Node.js 23.x and 25.x are not supported.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git
cd rakazo
cp .env.example .env
```

Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`,
then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own
`rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner
([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to
independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated
`SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported
model provider during onboarding.

For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true`
in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically;
`DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime.

Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the
`PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream
Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server, Treg endpoint, or OpenAPI JSON document from
**Integrations** without enabling either managed catalog. Connector credentials are encrypted on the
server and are never returned by the API.

Treg is usage-metered. Self-hosters supply their own Treg token; operators embedding Treg in a
hosted product should review [Treg's integration terms](https://treg.to/integrate.md), which require
a written agreement for hosted resale.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm sandbox:build
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a
local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies
migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main
doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible,
so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by
another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and
`API_PORT` to choose ports yourself.

To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which
publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \
  up postgres -d
```

Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the
user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in
place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is
disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state.

Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create
your first bot.

For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the
[self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md),
[backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md).

To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`.
Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and
`CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`,
and `desktop:1`.

To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`
and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment
explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment.
Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient
for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider
currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a
personal account token.
The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain
can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the
same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a
dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes,
separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use.
The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable
home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox.
Railway sandbox usage is metered.
New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example
`asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start.
Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit.

## Desktop and mobile

The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app.

With the development stack running, launch Electron with:

```bash
pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev
```

On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing
server. **This computer** installs and starts the published images with Docker Compose (the same
files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory, so Docker Desktop,
OrbStack, or Docker Engine must be installed; the app links to them when it is not. Installed
builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running
`pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` instead. Public servers
must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The
app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that
instance. The stack keeps running after the app quits; **Stop Local Stack** in the application
menu turns it off.

On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (`libfuse.so.2`). Distributions
that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show
`dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`. Install the FUSE 2 library (`fuse-libs` on Fedora,
`libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04, `libfuse2` on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without
FUSE:

```bash
chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage
./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run
```

name: FreeToken
description: FreeToken brings datacenter-scale model serving to your desktop. Run massive models locally, fast and efficiently.
readme_content:
| Download | Paper | Developer Slack | Community Discord | Community WeChat |

Unlock datacenter-class intelligence on the hardware you already own — Run 290B+ frontier MoE models locally on your gaming PC at blistering interactive speeds. ## About FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal and consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources—GPUs, CPUs, host memory, and interconnects—as a unified, elastic inference platform. Its core features include: - **Fast Edge-Native Runtime**: Provides efficient MoE serving with bandwidth-adaptive CPU–GPU co-execution ($q^\star$ policy), full-layer double-buffered prefill streaming, global LRU expert caching, graph-compatible execution, and the FTW fast weight format. - **Semantic-Aware Caching**: Features semantic anchor checkpoints for recurrent state and KV caches, allowing agentic context edits (e.g., tool calls, thinking blocks) to avoid redundant context recomputation. - **Elastic Memory Management**: Supports dynamic, runtime VRAM re-allocation between expert caches and KV memory without engine restarts or weight reloading. - **Broad MoE & Ecosystem Support**: Supports frontier open-weight MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GLM-5.2) across various parameter scales and quantization formats (e.g., MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, BF16), with Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs for seamless integration with real-world coding and tool-calling agents (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness). - **Diverse Consumer Hardware**: Scales across consumer laptops, gaming desktops, and workstation GPUs, with native support for NVIDIA RTX 30, RTX 40, and RTX 50 series GPUs. ## Getting Started ### Desktop app Download FreeToken for Windows or Linux at [flashml.ai](https://www.flashml.ai/). It sets the engine up for you and gives you a GUI for running models, chatting, and tuning the engine.
### CLI Install FreeToken with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended) or pip: ```bash uv pip install "freetoken[accel]" ``` Or build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken.git && cd FreeToken uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[accel]" ``` For More details: - [Install FreeToken](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/install.md) - [Quick start](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md) - [Supported models](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/models.md) - [CLI reference](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/cli.md) - [Repairing old FTW checkpoints](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/ftw-hotfix.md) - [Diagnosing a checkpoint that fails to load](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/scripts/checkpoint_diagnose/README.md) ## Citation If you use FreeToken for your research, please cite our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16157): ```bibtex @article{yang2026freetoken, title={FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution}, author={Yang, Shuo and Fan, Xiaoze and Pan, Melissa and Xi, Haocheng and Wang, Zhe and Sun, Shanlin and Keutzer, Kurt and Han, Song and Zaharia, Matei and Xu, Chenfeng and Stoica, Ion}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.16157}, year={2026} } ``` ## Acknowledgment FreeToken was deeply inspired by [mini-sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang), and learned the design and reused code from the following projects: [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer), [flash-linear-attention](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention), [LightLLM](https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm) and [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). ## License [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/LICENSE).
manifest_content:
[build-system]
# torch must match the runtime range below: build isolation resolves this list on its
# own, and a mismatch links the C++ extensions against the wrong libtorch.
# setuptools floor: 77 is the first release that understands the PEP 639 `license`
# SPDX string and `license-files` below.
requires = ["setuptools>=77", "torch>=2.14,<2.15", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "freetoken"
# Single source of truth: python/freetoken/version.py (read via the attr directive below).
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Local MoE-offload LLM inference runtime with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "FlashML Team" }]
# No License:: classifier: setuptools>=77 rejects mixing one with the SPDX string above.
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Environment :: GPU :: NVIDIA CUDA",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
]
# Version ranges are floor=last-verified, ceiling=next-major (kept loose enough to
# resolve, tight enough to bar a silent breaking bump). These ranges are the contract;
# there is no lockfile.
dependencies = [
    "apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.13.post3", # pin it
    "einops>=0.8,<1",
    "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
    # slot_cache: the device-side LRU admission kernel behind the MoE expert cache.
    "flashlib==0.4.0", # pin it
    "huggingface_hub>=1.5,<2",
    "msgpack>=1.1,<2",
    "modelscope>=1.37,<2",
    "numpy>=2.0,<3",
    "openai>=2.0,<3",
    "partial-json-parser>=0.2,<1",
    "pillow>=10,<13",
    "prompt_toolkit>=3.0,<4",
    "pydantic>=2.9,<3",
    "pyzmq>=27,<28",
    "safetensors>=0.6,<1",
    # floor+ceiling: sglang-kernel 0.4.9 requires torch==2.14.1.
    # PyPI's torch 2.14.1 wheel is itself the cu130 build, so plain pip resolves
    # correctly from PyPI alone; uv additionally pins the index below.
    "torch>=2.14,<2.15",
    "torchvision>=0.29,<0.30",
    "tqdm>=4.66,<5",
    "transformers>=5.18,<5.19",
    # CUDA torch 2.14 resolves Triton 3.8; AMD's ROCm 7.14 image supplies its
    # gfx1201-enabled Triton 3.7 build. Keep both supported without replacing the
    # runtime-specific wheel selected by the PyTorch distribution.
    "triton>=3.6,<3.9; platform_system == 'Linux'",
    "uvicorn>=0.30,<1",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken"
Repository = "https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken"
Issues = "https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/issues"

[project.scripts]
ft = "freetoken.cli:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=6.0"]
# Native fused-kernel packages. Without them the runtime falls back to the pure-Triton
# kernels in freetoken.kernel.triton (and the 'triton' attention backend). Install
# `freetoken[accel]` for the full native fast path.
fi = ["flashinfer-python[cu13]==0.6.18.post1"]
# renamed from sgl-kernel at 0.4; still imports as `sgl_kernel`, so never co-install both
sgl = ["sglang-kernel==0.4.9"]
accel = ["freetoken[fi,sgl]"]
# NOTE: the Marlin W4A16 NVFP4 expert-GEMM path (sm_80-99) borrows vLLM's AOT wheel
# (vllm>=0.14,<0.15), which pins transformers>=4.56,<5 and so is INCOMPATIBLE with the
# core transformers>=5.5 requirement. It is therefore not a lockable extra and is left
# out of the default resolution — install it separately (`pip install 'vllm>=0.14,<0.15'`)
# in a dedicated environment when you specifically need the Marlin path.

# uv-only provenance pins — pip ignores this section and resolves from PyPI, which
# works: PyPI's torch 2.14.1 is the same cu130 build this index serves.
# `explicit = true` scopes the index to the one package that needs it
# (the torch index also mirrors stale copies of common deps, e.g. packaging<=24.1,
# which would otherwise shadow PyPI under uv's first-index strategy).
[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu130" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu130"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
explicit = true

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true
package-dir = {"" = "python"}

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "freetoken.version.__version__"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["python"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = ["csrc/**/*", "moe/configs/**/*.json", "third_party/*/LICENSE", "third_party/*/VERSION", "third_party/*/freetoken.patch"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
markers = [
    "slow: takes tens of seconds (big kernel sweeps, real-checkpoint reads); deselect with -m 'not slow'",
    "needs_weights: needs a real local checkpoint, gat

name: agent-browser
description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
readme_content:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0

name: octomind
description: Open-source AI coding agent and agent runtime: one binary, any model, MCP-native. Runs in terminal, CI, or as a daemon.
readme_content:
Open-source coding agent harness. One Rust binary, any model, every surface.

Interactive, stdin, daemon, WebSocket, or ACP — one binary, one config.
A supervising model plans and checks the work.
Policy lives in TOML guardrails, not approval prompts.

[![CI](https://github.com/Muvon/octomind/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Muvon/octomind/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/octomind?style=flat-square&color=7c3aed)](https://crates.io/crates/octomind) [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fmuvon%2Foctomind%2Fbadges%2Fcoverage.json&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/muvon/octomind/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-7c3aed?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/muvon/octomind?style=flat-square&color=7c3aed)](https://github.com/muvon/octomind/stargazers) [Website](https://octomind.run) · [Docs](https://octomind.run/docs/) · [Tap Registry](https://github.com/muvon/octomind-tap) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [Issues](https://github.com/muvon/octomind/issues)
--- Octomind is an open-source coding agent harness. It gives any LLM the tools to work in a repository — read and edit files, run shells, search code, delegate to sub-agents — through [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), and runs the result as an interactive CLI, a stdin pipe, a daemon, a WebSocket server, or an ACP agent in your editor. Most agents stop and ask a human before each risky step, which works at a keyboard and blocks everything in CI. Octomind writes that policy down as TOML guardrails and adds a supervising model that plans and checks the work, so the same session can run with nobody watching. On 25 tasks taken from merged pull requests it solved 24; OpenCode solved 19 with the same model at about twice the cost ([benchmarks](#benchmarks)). ## How It Works One diagram, the whole turn: what is assembled before the model sees the request, the tool loop, how a turn is allowed to end, and what carries over to the next session. - **What the model sees** is built once per user message, not per tool round: `AGENTS.md`, the skills whose rules match the prompt (standard `SKILL.md` folders), the tool bundles those skills need (they start their own MCP servers on demand), and the few past lessons that match. [Skills](doc/usage/15-skills.md) · [Learning](doc/usage/13-learning.md) - **Compression** folds older turns into a summary that cites content-addressed blocks; the raw messages stay in a per-session archive and the `recall` tool brings any block back verbatim as a normal tool result, so history is never rewritten and the prompt cache survives. [Compression](doc/usage/08-compression.md) - **Guards, hooks, validators** are deterministic and live in `.agents/guardrails.toml` plus scripts; they run before any model opinion. The optional intent check (`[supervisor.authorizer]`, off by default) adds one supervisor-model look after the guards and blocks a call only when it independently conflicts with what you asked for. [Guardrails](doc/usage/18-guardrails.md) - **The supervisor** is a second model (`[supervisor.model]`): it keeps the plan and reminds the model of the goal each turn, cuts oversized tool results down to the lines the task needs (copied, never retyped), and refuses a self-reported "done" until the evidence checks out. The loop check is a fixed heuristic: when the model repeats itself or stalls it gets one nudge, never a takeover. [Supervisor](doc/usage/14-supervisor.md) - **The decision model** (`[decision]`) is optional: a classifier that answers typed yes/no questions with a probability instead of prose. When set, the supervisor sends its cheap questions there — which lessons to recall, which skill to activate, which lines to keep, whether a completion claim holds — and keeps chat calls for writing. [Calibrated decisions](doc/use-cases/23-calibrated-checks-with-evaluate.md) - **Learning** extracts lessons after `/done` or at exit, in your own words, into files under `learning///`; later sessions recall the ones that match. With `[supervisor.learning.evolution]` enabled, recurring lessons become skill and guardrail candidates that run in shadow first, then an A/B trial against a control arm, and go active only when they beat it. [Learning](doc/usage/13-learning.md) ## Why Octomind? Built for the work that keeps going after you leave: - **Policy as code, not approval popups.** Deterministic [guardrails](doc/usage/18-guardrails.md) — pre-call guards, post-result hooks, post-turn validators — live in TOML and scripts, so they work in CI, daemons, and scheduled runs. - **Measured, not claimed.** All four agents ran stock on the same tasks with the same judge. Per-case table, artifacts, and a reproduction guide are in the [benchmarks](#benchmarks). - **Ready-made specialists.** `octomind run developer:general` pulls a packaged agent (prompt, model, MCP servers, tool permissions) from a [tap](doc/integration/04-tap-system.md). Publish your own with one repo. - **Sessions that stay sharp.** Adaptive [compression](doc/usage/08-compression.md) keeps long tasks moving without forgetting the task or your last few messages. - **Learns the project as you work.** Corrections and rules you state become lessons, quoted from your own words and scoped to the project and role, and come back in later sessions. Turn on [evolution](doc/usage/13-learning.md) and recurring lessons compile into skill and guardrail candidates, trialled against a control and kept only when they help. - **Any model, any budget.** Use Octomind Cloud or your own key (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama, and more), pick a model per role, and cap spend per request and per session. Over budget, a terminal session asks y/N; a non-interactive run stops with exit code 75. - **One config.** Models, tools, roles, guardrails, budgets: all TOML, no framework code. ```bash # Interactive octomind run developer:general # Non-interactive — CI, scripts, automation echo "Explain the auth module" | octomind run developer:general --format plain # Daemon — keep it alive, talk to it from another terminal echo "watch the build" | octomind run --name watcher --daemon --format jsonl octomind send --name watcher "run the test suite" ``` ## Quick Start **1. Install** (macOS, Linux): ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muvon/octomind/master/install.sh | bash ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muvon/octomind/master/install.ps1 | iex ``` On macOS, you can also install with Homebrew: ```bash brew install muvon/tap/octomind ``` **2. Get model access.** The fastest path is Octomind Cloud, which includes models and needs no configuration: ```bash octomind login ``` Prefer your own provider key? Skip login and export one (also `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`), then follow [Model access](#model-access) to point the config at it: ```bash export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your_key" ``` **3. Run a specialist** in your project: ```bash cd ~/your/project octomind run developer:general ``` You're now in a session with an agent that can read your code, run commands, and edit files. The interface is a plain line prompt with markdown rendering — no TUI to learn, so it works over SSH, in `tmux`, and in CI logs. The first time you run a specialist, it may install its tools and ask for credentials. > `developer:general` comes from the default tap [`muvon/tap`](https://github.com/muvon/octomind-tap), not your local config. Plain `octomind run` starts the config's default role, `assistant:concierge`. Try the [recorded bug-fix demo](examples/fix-a-bug): two failing tests, an agent fix, and an independent test rerun. ## Benchmarks Measured on [octobench](https://github.com/Muvon/octobench) against **25 tasks harvested from merged pull requests** across Python, PHP, Rust, C++, and JavaScript. Each agent works in the pre-fix repo; held-out tests from the merged fix decide pass or fail. These are the published July 30, 2026 results, not a measurement of this checkout. | | solved | judge Σ / 2500 | cost | wall time | |---|---|---|---|---| | **octomind + glm-5.2** | **24/25** | **2264** | $63.43 | 3.6h | | claude code + claude-opus-5 | 23/25 | 2262 | $81.79 | 6.7h | | codex + gpt-5.6-sol | 21/25 | 2127 | $14.86 | 1.0h | | opencode + glm-5.2 | 19/25 | 2093 | $129.54 | 3.3h | - **The harness matters.** opencode used the same model and endpoint; octomind solved 24 vs 19 at roughly half the cost. All four agents ran stock invocations with no tuning, so this measures the whole harness, not individual features. - **Worst-case pricing, still ahead.** glm-5.2 ran without prompt caching while Opus billed ~97% of context re-reads at cache rates — and octomind still led on solves, cost, and wall time. - **Reproducible.** Per-case table, artifacts, and reproduction guide: [BENCHMARK.md](https://github.com/Muvon/octobench/blob/8aa39684ff6103782aacb1bd79ea98e96e50d6cf/BENCHMARK.md). Background: [blog post](https://octomind.run/blog/coding-agent-benchmark-real-prs). ## Guardrails: Policy as Code Drop a `.agents/guardrails.toml` in your repo. Octomind enforces it deterministically, with no code to compile and no plugin to install. ```toml # Pre-call deny — block a class of calls before they execute [[guard]] match = "shell(command=^rm\\s+-rf?)" message = "rm -rf blocked." # Conditional rule — only fires after the agent ran git status this session [[guard]] match = "shell(command=git push)" when = ["+shell(command=git status)"] message = "Review changes before pushing." ``` | Layer | When it runs | What it does | |---|---|---| | **Guards** | Before a tool call | Deny by capability, argument regex, and session history. A match returns a denial instead of executing the call. | | **Hooks** | After a tool result | A non-zero exit injects stdout into the agent's inbox — lint and format failures become automatic corrections without restarting the turn. | | **Validators** | After a turn | Scripts the agent reads on its next turn. This replaces "approve this change?" prompts in autonomous loops. | If you know Claude Code hooks: guards are `PreToolUse` denies declared in TOML, hooks are `PostToolUse`, validators are `Stop` — no scripts required for the common cases. Hook and validator script examples: [Guardrails guide](doc/usage/18-guardrails.md). ## One Harness, Five Surfaces The same harness, exposed wherever your workflow needs it. | Surface | Use it for | Docs | |---|---|---| | Interactive CLI | Daily work, any domain | [Sessions](doc/usage/05-sessions.md) | | Non-interactive (`--format plain` / `jsonl`) | CI, scripts, scheduled jobs | [CLI reference](doc/reference/01-cli-reference.md) | | Daemon + `send` | Background agents, continuous monitoring | [Daemon & hooks](doc/integration/03-daemon-and-hooks.md) | | WebSocket (`octomind server`) | IDE plugins, dashboards, integrations | [WebSocket server](doc/integration/01-websocket-server.md) | | ACP (`octomind acp`) | Agent inside Zed, JetBrains, VS Code, Neovim, or any ACP editor | [ACP protocol](doc/integration/02-ac

## Why Horizon? Good reads are scattered across feeds, forums, and timelines. Your attention isn't unlimited. Horizon collects, filters, and deduplicates them, then brings the worthwhile ones to you with context and community discussion. Your taste shapes what you read—and what you want from it. A news story calls for “why it matters”; an engineering deep dive calls for “what I can use.” Horizon's **profiles** give each kind of content its own scoring criteria and output, for a briefing that feels handpicked. ## Features - **📡 Bring Your Sources Together** — Follow RSS, Hacker News, Reddit, Telegram, X, GitHub, financial news, and more. - **🎯 Decide What's Worth Reading** — Define scoring rubrics with profiles, set individual thresholds, and merge repeated stories within each profile. - **🧩 Give Every Read the Right Treatment** — Choose summaries, context, solutions, or takeaways with Markdown prompts and JSON block definitions. - **💬 Go Beyond the Headline** — Add web-researched background and community discussion where they help explain the story. - **⚖️ Make Room for All Your Interests** — Cap the briefing's length and each category's share so one busy topic doesn't crowd out the rest. - **📬 Read Where You Already Are** — Generate English and Chinese briefings as Markdown, publish to Pages, or deliver by email and webhook. ### One Briefing, Different Ways to Read A profile is a reusable set of editorial rules: **what belongs, what's worth keeping, and what to write.** Built-in examples: | What you follow | Profile | What you get | |---|---|---| | Technology news | `tech-news` | Events and context, with impact and community discussion when useful | | Engineering deep dives | `tech-blog` | Background, solution, and practical takeaways | | AI creator material | `ai-creator` | A summary, with timely hooks and content angles when useful | Assign a profile to a source, or let AI choose. Want a different take? Adapt an existing profile—usually without changing Python. [Make a profile your own →](docs/profiles.md) ## How It Works ![Horizon architecture: ten sources feed a profile-driven pipeline with history and web search tools, delivering to Markdown, Pages, email, WeChat, and webhooks.](docs/assets/architecture.svg) [Editable OmniGraffle source](docs/assets/architecture.graffle) **Profiles define the treatment; runtime settings reflect your reading preferences.** Each item routes to one profile. Analysis, filtering, and deduplication happen before enrichment, then the selected items become a briefing grouped by profile. name: WeKnora
description: Open-source LLM knowledge platform: turn raw documents into a queryable RAG, an autonomous reasoning agent, and a self-maintaining Wiki.
readme_content:
English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Overview · Quick Start · What's New · Features · Clients · Docs · Development

## Overview [WeKnora](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com) is an open-source, LLM-powered knowledge framework for enterprise document understanding, semantic retrieval and reasoning. It brings a team's documents together so they can be searched, reasoned over and kept up to date. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de0e490a-e738-405e-bb3a-64b63edd7278

v0.9.0 · 2:45 · 1080p60 · English narration and subtitles

Use RAG to look things up, the agent for multi-step tasks, and the wiki to organize knowledge. All three work on the same knowledge bases. **The agent's toolbox.** Skills installed from ClawHub / SkillHub / Git / ZIP run in session-persistent Docker / E2B / Cube sandboxes, with an interactive terminal and graphical desktop beside the chat. Through the BrowserSkill extension the agent operates the user's own Chrome or Edge, and external MCP services (OAuth included) can be connected and enabled tool by tool. Beyond the three modes: - **Memory and curation**: cross-session long-term memory keeps the profile, preferences and facts a user has confirmed. Folder uploads keep their directory tree, and retrieval chunks can be edited, diffed and rolled back. - **Data sources and formats**: auto-sync from Feishu wiki / Feishu Drive / Confluence / GitLab / Tencent IMA / Notion / Yuque / DingTalk Docs / Seafile / RSS, with more on the way. 10+ document formats including PDF, Word, images, Excel and XMind; Office files are parsed in-process by anydoc. - **Channels and integrations**: Q&A in WeCom, Feishu, Slack, Telegram and other IM apps; an embed widget for external websites; a built-in MCP Server for Cursor, Claude and other AI tools; scoped API keys with a principal model for programmatic access. - **Models**: 29 built-in vendors with a generated model catalog, including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Zhipu, Hunyuan, Gemini, MiniMax, NVIDIA, LiteLLM and Ollama. - **Permissions and operations**: multi-workspace RBAC (four roles, per-resource ownership, per-workspace audit log), several storage instances per workspace, a runtime task-queue dashboard with worker-pool governance, and Langfuse tracing for agent steps, token usage and pipelines. - **Deployment**: LLMs, vector databases and storage backends are all swappable. Deploy locally or on a private cloud and keep the data in your own environment. ## Quick Start

ONLINE
WeChat Dialog Open Platform
Manage knowledge bases online and connect Q&A to Official Accounts, Mini Programs and other WeChat scenarios.

Open the platform →
CLOUD
Tencent Cloud Lighthouse
Deploy WeKnora from an application template and run it on your own cloud server.

Deploy on Tencent Cloud →
SELF-HOSTED
Your own environment
Deploy with Docker or Kubernetes and configure models, storage and networking yourself.

Run with Docker Compose ↓
### Run with Docker Compose Requires [Docker](https://www.docker.com/), [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/). ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora.git cd WeKnora cp .env.example .env # Edit .env as needed, see comments in the file docker compose pull # Pull the latest images docker compose up -d # Start core services ``` Then open **http://localhost** and follow the onboarding guide. A walkthrough with sample data is in the [Quickstart](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/03-quickstart). > [!TIP] > To use a local Ollama model, run `ollama serve > /dev/null 2>&1 &` first. For the Ollama embedding model name, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, and RAM notes, see [Configuration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/04-configuration). | Service | URL | |---------|-----| | Web UI | `http://localhost` | | Backend API | `http://localhost:8080` | | Langfuse Tracing | `http://localhost:3000` | ### Optional services Add `--profile` flags to enable additional components; multiple profiles can be combined. | Profile | Adds | |---------|------| | _(default)_ | Core services | | `full` | All features | | `neo4j` | Knowledge Graph (Neo4j) | | `minio` | Object Storage (MinIO) | | `langfuse` | Tracing (Langfuse) | ```bash docker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio pull docker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio up -d docker compose down # Stop services ``` ### Upgrading If you already have WeKnora running and downloaded a newer release: ```bash # Set WEKNORA_VERSION in .env to the target release (e.g. 0.9.0), or keep latest docker compose pull # Pull images matching WEKNORA_VERSION docker compose up -d # Recreate containers with new images ``` > [!NOTE] > `docker compose up -d` alone reuses locally cached images and may leave the UI version out of sync with the release you downloaded. Read the [upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#upgrade-notes) before upgrading. Deployments older than v0.8.2 should also read the [v0.8.2 notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#upgrade-notes). ### Other ways to deploy | Option | When to use it | |--------|----------------| | **Docker Compose** | The standard deployment above: all features, multiple services | | **Kubernetes (Helm)** | Production clusters; the chart is in [`helm/`](./helm) | | **Lite single binary** | Local or low-resource use with no external dependencies (SQLite + in-memory queue); see [Lite vs. standard](./docs/LITE.md) | | **Desktop app** | The Lite runtime with a GUI, login-free start and a macOS host sandbox; no installer is published yet, so build it from source | All options, hardware requirements and deployment topologies: [Installation guide](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/02-installation). > [!WARNING] > WeKnora ships with login authentication, but for production deployments we strongly recommend that you: > - deploy it in an internal / private network rather than on the public internet; > - avoid exposing the service directly to public networks, to prevent information leakage; > - configure proper firewall rules and access controls for the deployment environment; > - regularly update to the latest version for security patches and improvements. ## What's New ### v0.9.0 · 2026-10-29 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0) - **[WeKnora assistant](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#assistant)**: Ask about WeKnora releases, features and configuration, then work from the current page: create agents, schedule tasks and manage knowledge, acting as you within your permissions. - **[Multi-agent collaboration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#collaboration)**: Delegate independent subtasks, follow progress and bring the results together. - **[Automations](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#automations)**: Run one-off or recurring tasks with execution history, results and approval notifications. - **[Execution permissions](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#permissions)**: Read-only, confirm-before-change and automatic-write modes, with scoped session and automation grants. - **[Sandboxes and background work](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#sandbox)**: Optional per-user sandbox reuse, managed background shell jobs and skill rollout controls. - **[Parsing, sync and retrieval](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#knowledge)**: Configurable image pipelines, OCR preprocessing, deeper Feishu/Lark sync, Confluence PAT and retrieval improvements. - **[Upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#upgrade-notes)**: Review database migrations, Feishu resync, the sandbox allocation gate and configuration changes. ### v0.8.3 · 2026-10-14 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3)

name: open-duet
description: Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Claude Duet, OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, Instinct, Manus Cue: AI coworkers (named agents) with instructions, memory, routines, their own isolated computer, and your approval before they act.
readme_content:
# Open Duet **Build a team of AI coworkers and choose where they run.** Open Duet is an open-source workspace for creating named AI agents, giving them jobs and workspaces, and bringing them together to complete tasks. Keep useful context between conversations, run routines, and review actions before they make changes. Use the desktop app, run your own server, or visit the separate hosted service. Open Duet does not include an AI model or model subscription. You choose the engine and provider account used for your work. ## Project links - [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet) - [Desktop downloads](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/releases) - [Hosted app](https://suparagent.ai) - [Watch the demo](https://youtu.be/vtFy94DfETE) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Guides](#guides) - [Discord support](https://discord.com/invite/zpnuBRXhKg)

> **Status:** Open Duet is in active development. Desktop releases, self-hosting, > agent computers, and newer team features are still evolving. Review > [known limitations](#known-limitations) before relying on them for important work. ## Contents - [What you can do](#what-you-can-do) - [Ways to run Open Duet](#ways-to-run-open-duet) - [Hosted plans](#hosted-plans) - [Engines, data, and costs](#engines-data-and-costs) - [Known limitations](#known-limitations) - [Support](#support) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## What you can do - **Create agents and teams.** Give agents a name, role, engine, workspace, memory, and approval settings. A lead can delegate work to specialists or coordinate agents in shared rooms. Team leads can use Claude or Codex. See [teams and delegated work](docs/TEAMS.md). - **Keep useful context.** Agents can save notes, recall relevant notes and conversations, and search their history. You can review and edit what they remember. See [memory](docs/MEMORY.md). - **Run work on a schedule.** Create routines for scheduled, webhook, or manual runs. Review each result and answer requests for approval; a routine never approves an action by itself. See [routines](docs/ROUTINES.md). - **Choose how much freedom agents have.** Use Ask first, Accept edits, Approve for me (Claude, Codex, and Cursor), or Plan only. Review tool activity and approval decisions in the app. - **Connect tools and apps.** Connect services such as GitHub, Gmail, and Google Calendar through your own Composio key, then grant access to selected Claude or Codex agents. Changes wait for your approval. Add individual tools from the MCP Marketplace. See [connected apps](docs/CONNECTED_APPS.md). - **See what needs your attention.** The Today view gathers approvals, questions, routine outcomes, engine failures, and due tasks. It can show read-only Gmail and calendar items. See [everyday features](docs/EVERYDAY.md). - **Plan and follow work.** Use a task board and calendar to assign work, schedule one-time runs, and review conversations and attempts. See [tasks and calendar](docs/TASKS.md). - **Reuse instructions.** Save skills and start agents from templates. Skills are instructions you choose for a message. See [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [templates](docs/TEMPLATES.md). - **Use it from your phone.** Pair the phone app with your own server to chat, stop an answer, allow or deny a tool call, or create and edit agents and rooms. See the [phone app guide](docs/MOBILE.md). - **Work with files and history.** Search conversations, attach text and images, import audio for transcription with your consent and credentials, browse or download workspace files, and export your history. ## Ways to run Open Duet | | Desktop app | Self-hosted server | Hosted web app | Development checkout | |---|---|---|---|---| | Best for | A personal workspace on your computer | Keeping your agents and routines available on a server you control | Using the separately operated Suparagent service | Contributing or changing Open Duet | | Where workspace data lives | Your computer | Your server | An account-specific hosted workspace | Your development machine or configured database | | Start here | [Quick start](#quick-start) | [Self-hosting guide](docs/SELF-HOSTING.md) | [suparagent.ai](https://suparagent.ai) | [Development setup](docs/SETUP.md) | | Main requirements | Node.js 22+, uv, and an engine | Linux server, HTTPS, Docker or Node.js and uv, and an engine | An account and an AI provider account | Node.js, uv, and Docker if you use PostgreSQL | | Status | Experimental | Experimental; single owner | Separate hosted product | — | The hosted service is separate from the open-source desktop and self-hosted core. Hosted account, workspace, and billing data are handled by Suparagent; see the hosted service's [Privacy Policy](https://suparagent.ai/privacy) and [Terms](https://suparagent.ai/terms). ## Hosted plans The hosted preview lets you use your own Boat key for sandbox compute. Paid plans use compute operated by Suparagent, so you do not need to supply a Boat key. In both cases, you bring your AI provider account and pay that provider for model usage. | Plan | Monthly Suparagent price | Included running compute | Machine disk capacity | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Free preview | $0 | Billed to your Boat account | Small profile | | Starter | $15 | 100 hours per billing period | 51 GB | | Standard | $49 | 300 hours per billing period | 51 GB | | Pro | $99 | 720 hours per billing period | 111 GB | Paid-plan compute hours count while the sandbox is running, including idle time. At the limit, it stops until the next billing period or a plan change; compute overages are not charged. The disk value is the selected machine's capacity, not a separate storage quota. A stopped sandbox's disk is subject to the provider's retention period, so export important files before a paid plan ends. Paid checkout is enabled for hosted accounts; see the [Suparagent pricing page](https://suparagent.ai/pricing/) for current plans. ## Engines, data, and costs Connect an engine you already use: Claude Code or Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Google Gemini through Antigravity, Cursor, another command-line agent using the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), OpenRouter, or an OpenAI-compatible API such as Ollama or LM Studio. Available tools vary by engine; image input and agent computers, for example, are not supported by every engine. See [engine setup and capabilities](docs/ENGINES.md). For desktop and self-hosted use, conversations, agent notes, routines, and settings are stored in that instance's local data folder or server database. Workspace files stay in the folders you assign to agents. API keys saved through Open Duet are encrypted there; command-line sign-ins remain with the engine installed on that machine. When an agent answers, the selected engine receives the prompt and the context needed for that turn. This can include text you attach, relevant notes, and workspace content the engine reads. If the engine is a hosted service, that information is handled under that provider's terms. You bring the provider account, CLI sign-in, or API key; model usage may cost money. ## Quick start The desktop app runs from a source checkout. It needs Node.js 22 or newer, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and at least one engine available on the same computer. For a CLI engine, install it and sign in before opening Open Duet. You can also configure an API-based engine in **Settings → Engines**. Docker is only needed for the optional isolated agent computers. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet.git cd open-duet/desktop npm run app ``` On first launch, choose an engine, workspace, and approval mode. Then: 1. Open **Settings → Engines** and confirm an engine is ready. 2. Create an agent with a name, a clear job, and a workspace. 3. Start a chat. Choose **Ask first** to pause for approval before actions that need it. 4. Add teammates or create a routine when you want to split up or repeat work. See the [Releases page](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/releases) for current desktop installers and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for changes. Installers are experimental and unsigned. The assisted update flow offers a SHA-256-verified installer for you to open; it does not install updates automatically. The release-to-release update path has not been verified end to end. ## Example: prepare a weekly project briefing Create a lead agent and specialists, such as a researcher and an editor. Give them the same project workspace, and set the lead's engine to Claude or Codex. Ask the lead to prepare a briefing from the notes and reports in that folder. The lead can split the request into smaller tasks and hand them to the specialists. Their work runs in separate conversations, then returns to the lead to assemble. Follow along in chat and approve actions when the settings require it. Once the process works well, make it a weekly routine and review each run in the app. ## Scheduling tasks Routines run prompts on local agents on a schedule, by webhook, or on demand. They run in the backend, so the backend must stay running. The original Telegram bot and [Boat](https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys) sandbox task flow are optional and separate from the agent workspace. See [backend scheduling details](backend/README.md#scheduling) and [environment settings](backend/.env.example). ## Known limitations - Open Duet is early and changing. The self-hosted server is experimental and intended for one owner with paired devices, not a multi-user organization. - Team delegation is new; lead agents need to use Claude or Codex. - The phone app has been tried on an Android emulator and an Android phone, not on iOS. It has no push notifications or store release. - Docker computers, browser tools, and the macOS native desktop preview are experimental and opt-in. - Desktop installers are unsigned and have limited platform verification. See [desktop setup details](docs/SETUP.md#desktop-app-from-a-source-checkout-experimental). - Connected apps are reached through Composio and tested against a fake Composio service, not yet the real service. Only Claude and Codex agents can use them, and changes wait for your approval. - The MCP Marketplace, hosted cloud computers, quiet routine results, and audio transcription have not had live-service or packaged-app qualification. ## Guides **Getting started** - [First-run setup and approvals](docs/SETUP.md) - [Engines and models](docs/ENGINES.md) - [Self-hosting](docs/SELF-HOSTING.md) **Agents and work** - [Teams and delegated work](docs/TEAMS.md) - [Agent settings and chat management](docs/CHAT_MANAGEMENT.md) - [Memory and context](docs/MEMORY.md) - [Routines](docs/ROUTINES.md) - [Tasks and calendar](docs/TASKS.md) - [Everyday features](docs/EVERYDAY.md): search, attachments, audio, and Today **Tools and customization** - [Connected apps](docs/CONNECTED_APPS.md) - [App language settings](docs/LOCALIZATION.md) - [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [templates](docs/TEMPLATES.md) - [Agent computers](docs/COMPUTERS.md), [native desktop](docs/NATIVE-DESKTOP.md), and [browser tools](docs/BROWSER.md) - [Features](docs/FEATURES.md) and [capability matrix](docs/CAPABILITIES.md) **Project** - [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [Phone app](docs/MOBILE.md) - [Contributing](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Support - Join the [Open Duet Discord community](https://discord.com/invite/zpnuBRXhKg) for questions and discussion. - Report bugs and request features in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/issues). - For hosted account or billing questions, use the contact link on [suparagent.ai](https://suparagent.ai/contact

name: pstack-claude
description: Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Muse, OpenCode, Pi, and Prime Agent versions of Poteto's pstack. Rigorous agent workflows with Cursor primitives translated for other harnesses.
readme_content:
# pstack [![Buy Me A Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20A%20Coffee-support-yellow?logo=buy-me-a-coffee&logoColor=white)](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer) [![Mentioned in Awesome Claude Code](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge.svg)](https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code) Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Built for Claude Code This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. [Upstream's Claude Code install](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/c742dd6/harness/pstack/claude-code) asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to `poteto-mode`. ## Install
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open the **Marketplaces** tab, select `pstack-claude`, and choose **Enable auto-update**. To update once by hand, run `claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude`.
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ``` Invoke a skill by typing `$` and its name, such as `$poteto-mode` or `$babysit`, then choosing its entry, which inserts `$pstack:`. `/skills` lists every skill.
Pi Run in your terminal: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.
Muse Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack muse plugins approve pstack ``` The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its `SessionStart` hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with `/` (for example `/poteto-mode`), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.
Kimi Code CLI After a release containing `kimi.plugin.json` is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session: ```text /plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude /reload ``` To test an unreleased checkout, use `/plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude` instead, followed by `/reload`; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run `/reload`. Invoke a skill as `/skill:pstack:poteto-mode`; see the [Kimi mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/kimi-tools.md) for tool guidance.
Grok Build ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust grok plugin enable pstack ``` Start a new session and use `/poteto-mode` to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect `grok plugin details pstack` and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run `grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data`, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. `grok plugin update` does not refresh a local install.
MiniMax Code Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins" cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack" ``` MiniMax Code loads each directory under `plugins/` in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. `mcode plugin list` shows it as `pstack@local`. To update after a `git pull`, delete the old `plugins/pstack` copy first, then run the `cp` line again; copying onto an existing copy nests it inside.
Antigravity (agy) Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack ``` This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (`skills`, `agents`, and `SessionStart` routing hook) into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack`.
Other harnesses OpenCode (the CLI and the desktop app), Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")" test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target" done ``` To update, run `git pull` in the clone, then run the `for` loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for `poteto-mode` by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See [shared installation](docs/reference.md#shared-skills-installation) for per-harness notes and uninstalling.
### Configure pstack routes tasks to `poteto-mode` automatically. At session start, a hook injects an instruction that points the agent at it: the plugin's hook on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and MiniMax Code, and the pstack extension on Pi. Codex runs the hook only after you trust it through `/hooks`, and Muse only after `muse plugins approve pstack`. Other harnesses have no hook. Run `setup-pstack` to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (`arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max`). ## Getting started ```text Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages. ``` For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses `how` and `why` to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in `architect` before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence. [Other playbooks](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md#playbooks) cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects. ![poteto-mode on Claude Code, Codex, and Pi turns a request into verified work. Choose a playbook, plan and delegate with architect, arena, or swarm, then review and verify with interrogate, tests, and measurements. Project playbooks customize the workflow, and setup-pstack configures the model and reasoning effort per role. Supporting skills include how, why, and unslop.](assets/pstack-overview.png) ## Details - [Skills and slash commands](docs/reference.md#slash-commands) - [Runtime setup](docs/reference.md#runtime-support) - [Models and dependencies](docs/reference.md#configuration-and-dependencies) - [Maintenance and port scope](docs/reference.md#maintenance) ## Data handling pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login. ## Contributing Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). To support maintenance of this port, [buy the maintainer a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer). ## License This port, including its modifications and additions, is also [MIT-licensed](LICENSE), © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See [LICENSE-cursor-team-kit](LICENSE-cursor-team-kit), [LICENSE-thermos](LICENSE-thermos), and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

name: go-music-dl
description: 一个基于 Go 语言的全网音乐搜索与下载工具。支持 CLI 命令行与 Web 服务双模式，内置网易云、QQ、酷狗、Bilibili、汽水音乐等 10+ 个主流平台，支持多源并发搜索与无损音质解析。music-dl交流群：755087923
readme_content:
# Go Music DL > ⭐ 如果这个项目对你有帮助，欢迎点一个 Star。

Go Music DL 是一个多平台音乐搜索与下载工具，支持 **Web**、**TUI** 和**桌面端**，覆盖单曲、歌单、专辑、排行榜与本地音乐。它同时暴露了一套 AI 可调用的接口——**AI 可以直接操控你正开着的网页播放器**，点歌、切歌、暂停、调音量都不用你动手，详见 [AI / Agent 调用](#ai--agent-调用)。 ## 🚀 快速开始 ### 桌面端 / 移动端 从 [Releases](https://github.com/guohuiyuan/go-music-dl/releases) 下载对应安装包： - Windows / Linux / macOS：从 Releases 下载 `music-dl-desktop-rust` 或 `music-dl-desktop-go` 对应平台包，解压后直接运行。 - Android：优先下载 `music-dl_arm64-v8a.apk`，已内置 FFmpeg，无需额外安装。 - iOS：使用 `music-dl-ios-unsigned.ipa` 自行签名。 ### Web / TUI ```bash # Web，默认访问 http://localhost:8080/music ./music-dl web # 挂载到反向代理二级目录 ./music-dl web --base-path /dl # 终端搜索 ./music-dl -k "周杰伦" ``` Web 的搜索、试听、下载和歌单浏览无需登录；修改设置或 Cookie 时才需要管理员账号。首次配置时，启动日志会打印 `Web setup token`，用它创建管理员账号即可。TUI 常用键：`↑/↓` 移动、`空格` 选择、`a` 全选、`r` 换源、`Enter` 下载、`w` 每日推荐、`q` 退出。 ### Docker ```bash docker compose up -d --pull always --remove-orphans ``` 访问 `http://localhost:8080`。首次启动会自动创建 `./data` 并配置好容器写权限；Compose 不依赖仓库里的 Dockerfile 或其他文件，只需 `docker-compose.yml` 和镜像即可启动。修改源码后可使用 `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build` 本地构建。 ### AI / Agent 调用 Web 服务提供 AI 能力索引和播放器控制接口。搜索、歌单、专辑、排行榜、歌单分类、换源、歌词、下载和本地音乐等能力全部复用现有的 `/music/*` 接口，不再维护第二套 AI 包装路由。 ```bash # 搜索歌曲，只请求 QQ 和网易云 curl "http://localhost:8080/music/search?q=周杰伦&type=song&sources=qq&sources=netease" ``` API 索引：`http://localhost:8080/music/api/ai/index`，精简说明：`http://localhost:8080/music/llms.txt`。索引会列出可直接复用的现有搜索、详情、排行榜、歌单分类、换源、下载和本地音乐接口，以及新增的播放器控制接口。 #### AI 可以直接操控网页播放器 只要浏览器里开着本站页面，AI 就能**远程操作这个页面**：点歌、切歌、暂停、调音量、拖动进度，全部靠一条 HTTP 请求完成。不需要浏览器自动化、不需要模拟点击、也不需要接管你的鼠标键盘。 原理是页面自己维持着一条 SSE 长连接（`GET /music/api/ai/player/events`）：AI 把命令 POST 到服务端，服务端推给在线的页面，页面执行后把播放状态回传。所以 AI 看到的 `playing`、`position`、`current` 都是页面的真实状态，而不是猜测。 典型对话：**“帮我放一首 ClariS 的歌”** → AI 调 `/music/search` 找歌 → 调 `/api/ai/player/play` 点播 → 轮询 `/api/ai/player/state` 确认已经在放。 ```bash # 1. 看看当前有哪些播放器在线、在放什么 curl "http://localhost:8080/music/api/ai/player/state" # 2. 直接点播（用 id + source，或只给 query 让服务端自己搜第一首） curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/music/api/ai/player/play" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest" \ -d '{"id":"1958384591","source":"netease","name":"ALIVE","artist":"ClariS"}' # 3. 传输控制 curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/music/api/ai/player/command" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest" \ -d '{"action":"pause"}' ``` `/api/ai/player/command` 支持 `play`、`pause`、`toggle`、`stop`、`next`、`previous`、`seek`、`volume` 和 `rate`。没有已打开的播放器时会返回 `409 player_not_connected`。 #### 多客户端：各控各的 每个打开的页面（标签页、桌面端、另一台设备）都是独立客户端，**状态互不覆盖，命令互不串台**： * 连接时带 `?client_id=xxx` 声明身份；老页面匿名连上来后，第一次上报状态时会被自动认领。 * `POST /play` 和 `/command` 带 `client_id` 就只投给那一台；只有 1 台在线时自动定向，一条 curl 照样能用。 * **多台在线又不带 `client_id`** → 返回 `409 ambiguous_client` 和候选列表，绝不并发让所有页面一起切歌。 * `GET /state` 不带参数时优先选择在线、正在播放、页面可见的客户端，同类按连接顺序稳定选择，不会被 2 秒一次的状态上报带着来回跳；`GET /state?client_id=xxx` 精确读取某一台。 * 每台客户端分别保存 `last_command`，查询某台不会混入其他客户端的命令。 * 页面关掉后不会立刻消失，而是标记 `connected:false` 并保留最后状态 10 分钟；定向投给它返回 `409 client_not_connected`。 * 在线事件流最多 64 个；命令通道写满时返回 `503 player_busy`，不会假装投递成功。 **使用前提：** 页面必须处于打开状态（后台标签页也能收命令，但浏览器会节流定时器，进度上报会变慢）；升级后请 `Ctrl+F5` 硬刷新，`app.js` 是编译进二进制的，旧页面用不了 `client_id` 定向。这套接口默认无鉴权，仅靠 `X-Requested-With` 做 CSRF 防护，**请勿把服务直接暴露到公网**；远程使用请走 SSH 隧道或放在反向代理的鉴权后面。 --- ![Web UI 1](./screenshots/web1.png) ![Web UI 2](./screenshots/web2.png) ![TUI 1](./screenshots/tui1.png) ![TUI 2](./screenshots/tui2.png) ## 主要功能 * **多端使用**：Web、TUI 终端和原生桌面应用，桌面端自动启动内置服务。 * **搜索与下载**：多平台聚合搜索单曲、歌单和专辑，支持试听、批量下载、换源和无损音频。 * **歌单管理**：浏览官方分类、个人歌单和排行榜，也可创建本地歌单并跨平台收藏歌曲。 * **登录能力**：支持 Cookie 与扫码登录，用于个人歌单、更高音质和部分受限资源。 *
